en: The Philippine eagle is the largest eagle in the Philippines, reaching a body length of up to one meter.
The Philippines declared independence on June 12, 1898, ending exactly 377 years of Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippine Senate is composed of 24 elected senators who serve a single term of six years.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English serve as the two official national languages.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, built by the Ifugao people 2,000 years ago, are carved into mountains at 1,500 meters above sea level.
Filipino pediatrician Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that kept 50 premature babies warm without using electricity.
Jose Rizal was a polyglot who spoke 22 different languages, including Spanish, Latin, and Japanese, before his execution.
The Philippine flag features eight rays on the sun, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish rule.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote, and at least 35 years old to run for president.
The Paoay Church in Ilocos Norte features 24 massive buttresses designed to protect the structure from severe earthquakes.
A traditional Philippine jeepney is stretched to exactly 18 feet long to accommodate up to 20 seated passengers.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu attracts over two million visitors annually to celebrate the Santo Niño.
